text:
sara: FYI escalation from Matt — customer saw a ~10x latency and billing spike. They reported many retries (429/502) from our hosted API. Looks tied to their Flask app creating the async client at import time. Logs pasted below.

matt-customer: sending logs from prod (sanitized):
```
Jun 23 10:12:01 app gunicorn[1234]: starting worker process pid=4567
Jun 23 10:12:03 app web.1: WARNING httpx._client: TLS handshake took 2.3s for host api.redwood.example
Jun 23 10:12:04 app web.1: ERROR redwood: request failed status=502 attempt=1
Jun 23 10:12:04 app web.1: ERROR redwood: retrying request attempt=2
Jun 23 10:12:06 app web.1: WARNING httpx._client: TLS handshake took 1.9s
Jun 23 10:12:06 app web.1: INFO billing: tokens_charged=2400 requests=300
```

matt-customer: environment: python 3.10, gunicorn 20.1, preload_app=True, redwood-py==0.11.0rc1, httpx==0.23.0

sara: they said latency spikes line up with deploys (preload + forking). can someone triage?

kevin-sdk: on it. quick question: are they instantiating an AsyncClient at module import? that pattern usually triggers connection pool/TLS setup in main thread which gets inherited and can cause weird handshake timings after fork. can you paste the init code?

matt-customer: minimal repro from customer:
```python
# myapp/client.py
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient(api_key="***")  # created at import time

# app.py
from flask import Flask
from myapp.client import client
app = Flask(__name__)

@app.route('/')
async def index():
    return await client.generate("hi")
```
They said they used gunicorn --preload so client created before workers fork.

eva-infra: yep, preload + AsyncClient at import is a red flag. fork semantics + async state (sockets, ssl sessions) are tricky. Did they try without preload or creating the client per-worker?

matt-customer: they switched preload off as a test and saw latencies drop by ~40% on first requests but still occasional slow handshakes.

kevin-sdk: repro notes: httpx/OpenSSL can perform TLS handshake on connection creation, and if a client/connection pool is created pre-fork it can lead to inherited fds/state that trigger retries/timeouts in child processes. Two things:
- short-term workaround: create the AsyncClient lazily in an async startup hook or inside the worker process, not at module import. e.g.
```python
# prefer this
client = None
async def get_client():
    global client
    if client is None:
        client = await AsyncClient.create(api_key="...")  # pseudocode
    return client
```
- alternate: use sync client (redwood.Client) in sync Flask endpoints or move to ASGI server (uvicorn) to avoid gunicorn preload + asyncio mismatch.

kevin-sdk: also asking them to try pinning httpx to 0.24.x + our patched redwood-py 0.11.1 (we pushed a small fix that delays connection pool bootstrap until first request). 0.11.0rc1 will eagerly create a pool on init.

matt-customer: quick test with our patched 0.11.1 — initial numbers look better. initial handshake still ~300ms occasionally but not multiple seconds and retries dropped. billing spike gone. thanks.

sara: can eng add a regression test for 'async client pre-fork init' to the SDK test matrix and a note in docs about gunicorn preload? requester wants a patch release if possible.

kevin-sdk: will open SDK ticket and add tests. also adding a doc blurb to the Flask quickstart recommending not to create AsyncClient at import time when using gunicorn --preload, and to prefer per-worker initialization.

matt-customer: will confirm with customer tomorrow and share full logs. thanks all. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: [notice] release redwood-py@0.11.1 pushed to staging by kevin-sdk

kevin-sdk: follow-up action items: 1) SDK ticket #12345 (add test + lazy pool) 2) Docs PR to /docs/integrations/flask.md 3) Patch release 0.11.1 (in progress). please DM me logs if anyone has variants.

sara: marking escalated->resolved for now pending customer confirmation.

matt-customer: customer confirmed next day: no billing spike after patch. closing the loop.
